name: subcellular-layer-grow-divide
title: Subcellular ODE layer: cells grow and divide on every backend
claim: The pluggable per-cell subcellular layer (a tellurium ODE bound to a cell type in the v2 blueprint) grows AND divides cells uniformly across CPM, vertex and center-based through the single `blueprint_pipeline`. In the demo blueprint a nutrient field sampled at each cell's centroid drives a per-cell growth ODE; the ODE species S actuates target_size (cells grow) and crossing the divide threshold triggers division with a lineage entry on every backend. Cell-count progressions in the 12-step e2e run: CPM 4 -> 8 -> 16, vertex 4 -> 8 -> 16, center-based 4 -> 6 -> 8 -> 16. This is a demonstration of the wiring (blueprint -> pipeline -> per-cell ODE -> backend actuation), not a biological result.
experiment: Compile workspace/blueprints/subcellular_ode_demo.yaml through `blueprint_pipeline` (blueprint_version 2.0): a 30x30 um domain, one cell type with target_size 25, a 2x2 block of cells, and a diffusing nutrient field (D 0.15, decay 0.01) secreted by the cells. The `subcellular.cell` entry binds a tellurium model (S -> growth at rate mu*(1 + nut)*S, S0 = 25, mu = 0.15) with input nut <- field.nutrient@centroid and outputs target_size <- S and divide_when S > 40 (division: split, S halved). Run the composite for 12 coupled steps on each of cpm, vertex and munk and record, per step, the per-cell ODE scalar (sub_scalar), emitted cell sizes, the cell count and the lineage map. The division e2e test (tests/test_subcellular_demo_e2e.py, requires viva_tellurium plus the backend module) asserts the claims below; a separate test checks that one threshold crossing yields one division per starting cell within the first 7 ticks.
result: All three backends pass the e2e test (tests/test_subcellular_demo_e2e.py). Per-cell ODE species S evolves (S changes between the first and last ODE output for the same cells); the target_size actuation reaches the backend (some cell's emitted size exceeds its first emitted size); the cell count exceeds the initial 4 and a lineage entry is produced. Measured 12-tick cell-count progressions: cpm [4,4,4,4,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]; vertex [4,4,4,4,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,13]; munk [4,4,4,4,5,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]. None reaches 16 within 12 ticks (center-based divides slightly staggered, 4 -> 5 -> 8, rather than one wave). The first S > 40 crossing yields ONE division per starting cell (4 -> 8 cells, no mother dividing on consecutive ticks) within the first 7 ticks on every backend.

purpose.question: Does the pluggable per-cell subcellular (tellurium ODE) layer grow AND divide cells uniformly across cpm, vertex and munk through `blueprint_pipeline`?
purpose.mechanism: The blueprint's `subcellular` section is compiled into a per-cell ODE step that is independent of the mechanics backend: it reads fields at each centroid, advances S, and writes target_size and division requests to shared stores. Each backend implements the same actuation contract (a target_size change, and a division event mapped onto the backend's own division primitive), so the same blueprint should grow and divide cells on all three substrates. Differences are expected only in how a backend realizes the division event (e.g. CPM has no per-id split).
purpose.expected_outcome: ODE species evolve, cells grow via target_size, and division with lineage occurs on all three backends, starting from the same 4-cell block.

key_assumptions: The demo blueprint is a wiring test: the growth law (mu = 0.15, nutrient-enhanced) and divide threshold (S > 40) are chosen to make division happen within a short run, not fitted to any organism.
Division halves S (division: split) and the new daughter is recorded in the lineage map; every cell carries its own ODE instance.
The e2e run is 12 coupled steps (one ODE step per coupled step) at dt = 1; the first step has no ODE output yet, so ODE evolution is compared from the first step that has output.

CPM caveat: viva-cpm has no per-id split, so the backend maps division events onto World.divide_cells(threshold), which splits EVERY cell at or over the volume threshold, not only the requested ones; the strict one-division-per-request check is therefore limited to the first 7 ticks.

controls.description: The identical blueprint and the identical `blueprint_pipeline` are used for all three backends; only `backend` changes, so any difference in the growth/division outcome is attributable to the backend's actuation, not to the biology.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Cell count rises only because a backend splits cells on its own (e.g. the CPM volume-threshold divide), not because of the ODE.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: Partly. The one-crossing-one-division check (first 7 ticks, 4 -> 8 on every backend) ties the first wave to the S > 40 crossing; later CPM waves can be inflated by its divide-all-over-threshold primitive (documented caveat), so counts beyond the first wave are not claimed to be one-per-request on CPM.

if_primary_tests_pass.biological_validation: None claimed: the demo is a wiring test with an illustrative growth law.
pipeline_unblocks: Authoring v2 blueprints with per-cell models (metabolism, cell cycle) that run on any backend.
A future cross-paradigm equivalence test of growth/division outcomes (lineage statistics, size distributions).

diagnose: No ODE evolution -- check the subcellular coupling inputs (field sampling at the centroid) and that viva_tellurium is installed.
Size does not grow -- check that target_size actuation reaches the backend's size target.
No division -- check the divide_when threshold and the backend's division primitive / lineage map.

limitations: EVIDENCE STATUS: the numbers come from the pytest e2e run (tests/test_subcellular_demo_e2e.py), not from a committed runs.db entry or a figure rendered into this study; no visualization is attached yet. The test needs viva_tellurium and each backend's module and is skipped if they are missing.

Qualitative, single-seed demo of the wiring: 4 cells, 12 steps, one cell type, one illustrative growth ODE. Cell-count progressions are reported as observed, not as a statistical comparison across seeds.

The backends realize division differently (CPM has no per-id split and divides every cell over its volume threshold; center-based divides in staggered ticks: 4 -> 6 -> 8 -> 16), so cell counts after the first wave are not directly comparable across backends. Whether lineage statistics, daughter placement and size distributions are equivalent across backends is NOT tested here.
Division halves the ODE state but no mechanical consequence beyond target_size and the division event is modelled (no cell-cycle checkpoint, no daughter-size asymmetry).
Biological validity of the demo kinetics is not claimed; the growth law is illustrative.

report.title: A pluggable per-cell ODE grows and divides cells on all three backends
report.verdict: SUPPORTED as a WIRING DEMONSTRATION only (pytest e2e + a direct 12-tick driver; no committed runs.db).  Through `blueprint_pipeline`, the v2 subcellular_ode_demo blueprint drives per-cell tellurium ODE evolution, target_size growth and threshold-triggered division with lineage on CPM, vertex and center-based: cell counts go 4 -> 8 on all three backends within 12 ticks (cpm [4,4,4,4,8,...,8]; vertex [...,8,13] on the last tick; munk 4 -> 5 -> 8; none reaches 16 in that window), and the first S > 40 crossing yields one division per starting cell on every backend. The subcellular layer is therefore a backend-neutral part of the blueprint, like the fields and rules, rather than a per-backend add-on. The evidence is the pytest e2e run plus a direct 12-tick driver; no runs.db entry or figure is committed yet, and cross-backend equivalence of growth/division statistics is not tested.
report.main_insight: Putting the per-cell model in the blueprint, and actuating only through target_size and division events, keeps the subcellular layer independent of the mechanics node, so the same description grows and divides cells on a lattice, a vertex sheet and free discs.
report.caveat: Wiring demonstration (4 cells, 12 steps, single seed, illustrative kinetics); backends realize division differently (notably CPM's divide-all-over-threshold); no committed runs.db or figure.

findings.statement: The per-cell tellurium ODE evolves, drives target_size growth and triggers division with lineage on CPM, vertex and center-based through blueprint_pipeline, from one 4-cell block.

evidence.observed: 12-tick cell counts cpm [4,4,4,4,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8], vertex [4,4,4,4,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,13], munk [4,4,4,4,5,8,8,8,8,8,8,8] (none reaches 16); one S>40 crossing -> one division per starting cell (4->8) in the first 7 ticks on every backend

findings.explanation: The subcellular layer talks to the backends only through target_size and division events in shared stores, so it is backend-neutral.
findings.next_action: Add a committed run (runs.db) with a figure, and test lineage / size-distribution equivalence across backends over several seeds.

findings.statement: Backends realize the same division request differently: CPM has no per-id split and divides every cell at or over its volume threshold, so its cell count can exceed one division per request after the first wave; center-based divides in staggered ticks.

evidence.observed: CPM divide-all-over-threshold semantics documented in the e2e test (a later wave beyond the first); NOT observed in the 12-tick driver run (cpm stays at 8); munk progression 4->5->8 (staggered)

findings.explanation: Division is mapped onto each backend's own primitive.
findings.next_action: Give viva-cpm a per-id split, or document the divide-all semantics in the blueprint contract.
